antibacterial-drugs.moa: Classified by target: cell wall synthesis (penicillins, cephalosporins, vancomycin, carbapenems, bacitracin); cell membrane (polymyxins, daptomycin); protein synthesis (30S: aminoglycosides, tetracyclines; 50S: macrolides, chloramphenicol, clindamycin, linezolid); nucleic acids (quinolones, rifampicin, metronidazole); folate pathway (sulfonamides, trimethoprim)
antibacterial-drugs.uses: Treatment and prophylaxis of bacterial infection; choose by site, likely organism, sensitivity and patient factors; bactericidal drugs for endocarditis and meningitis; combinations to prevent resistance
antibacterial-drugs.adr: Allergy and anaphylaxis, GI upset, superinfection and Clostridium difficile colitis, resistance; drug-specific toxicity (nephrotoxicity, ototoxicity, tendon rupture and so on)
antibacterial-drugs.ci: Known hypersensitivity to the drug or class; reduce doses in renal or hepatic failure; avoid tetracyclines, quinolones, chloramphenicol and aminoglycosides in pregnancy; use the narrowest effective drug for the shortest time

sulfonamides.moa: Structural analogues of PABA that block dihydropteroate synthase and stop bacterial folate synthesis (bacteriostatic); trimethoprim in co-trimoxazole blocks the next step, dihydrofolate reductase, giving synergy
sulfonamides.uses: Urinary tract infection; co-trimoxazole for Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia, typhoid, nocardiosis; toxoplasmosis (with pyrimethamine); sulfacetamide eye drops; silver sulfadiazine for burns; sulfasalazine in colitis
sulfonamides.adr: Rash and Stevens-Johnson syndrome, crystalluria, nausea, haemolysis in G6PD deficiency, bone marrow suppression, kernicterus in neonates, hyperkalaemia (trimethoprim), photosensitivity
sulfonamides.ci: Sulfa allergy, G6PD deficiency, late pregnancy, newborns and infants under 2 months, severe renal and hepatic disease and porphyria; drink plenty of fluids

quinolone-antimicrobials.moa: Inhibit bacterial DNA gyrase (topoisomerase II) and topoisomerase IV, blocking DNA replication (bactericidal)
quinolone-antimicrobials.uses: Urinary tract infection, enteric fever, traveller's diarrhoea, prostatitis, bone and joint infection, respiratory infection (levofloxacin, moxifloxacin), anthrax, tuberculosis (second line), gonorrhoea; ciprofloxacin for Pseudomonas
quinolone-antimicrobials.adr: Nausea, diarrhoea, headache, dizziness, tendinitis and tendon rupture, QT prolongation, photosensitivity, seizures, hypo- and hyperglycaemia, C. difficile colitis, cartilage damage in children and peripheral neuropathy
quinolone-antimicrobials.ci: Pregnancy and children (relative), epilepsy, tendon disorders, myasthenia gravis and QT prolongation; avoid antacids, iron and calcium within 2 hours; may raise theophylline and warfarin levels

penicillins.moa: Bind penicillin-binding proteins and block peptidoglycan cross-linking in the cell wall, causing lysis (bactericidal); β-lactamase inhibitors (clavulanic acid, sulbactam, tazobactam) protect the penicillin from bacterial enzymes
penicillins.uses: Streptococcal and pneumococcal infection; syphilis (penicillin G, benzathine); rheumatic fever prophylaxis; meningococcal disease; endocarditis; cloxacillin and flucloxacillin for staphylococci; ampicillin and amoxicillin for respiratory and urinary infection; piperacillin for Pseudomonas
penicillins.adr: Hypersensitivity (rash to anaphylaxis, the most important), diarrhoea, C. difficile colitis, seizures with high doses, interstitial nephritis, Jarisch-Herxheimer reaction in syphilis; amoxicillin rash in infectious mononucleosis; benzathine penicillin: painful, never IV
penicillins.ci: Penicillin allergy (a few cross-react with cephalosporins); infectious mononucleosis (ampicillin); reduce doses in renal failure; probenecid prolongs the effect

cephalosporins.moa: Same as penicillins: block cell wall synthesis by binding penicillin-binding proteins; more resistant to many β-lactamases, with the spectrum widening from first (Gram-positive) to third and fourth generations (Gram-negative, and Pseudomonas with ceftazidime and cefepime)
cephalosporins.uses: Surgical prophylaxis (cefazolin); respiratory and urinary infection (cefuroxime, cefixime, cefpodoxime); meningitis, typhoid and gonorrhoea (ceftriaxone); pseudomonal infection (ceftazidime, cefepime); sepsis
cephalosporins.adr: Hypersensitivity, diarrhoea, C. difficile colitis, bleeding from vitamin K lack (cefoperazone, ceftriaxone), disulfiram-like reaction (cefoperazone), biliary sludge and kernicterus risk in neonates (ceftriaxone), thrombophlebitis
cephalosporins.ci: Serious allergy to penicillin or cephalosporin; ceftriaxone in neonates with jaundice and with calcium infusions; reduce the dose in renal failure

monobactam.moa: Aztreonam inhibits cell wall synthesis by binding penicillin-binding protein 3 of Gram-negative aerobic bacteria and is stable against many β-lactamases
monobactam.uses: Serious Gram-negative infection (Pseudomonas, Enterobacteriaceae), urinary and respiratory infection, sepsis in patients allergic to penicillins
monobactam.adr: Rash, diarrhoea, nausea, phlebitis and raised liver enzymes; low risk of allergy and little cross-reactivity (except with ceftazidime)
monobactam.ci: Aztreonam allergy; reduce dose in renal failure; not active against Gram-positive and anaerobic bacteria

carbapenems.moa: Bind penicillin-binding proteins and inhibit cell wall synthesis; very broad spectrum including Gram-negative, Gram-positive and anaerobic bacteria, and stable against most β-lactamases (including ESBL)
carbapenems.uses: Severe hospital infection, sepsis, intra-abdominal and pelvic infection, febrile neutropenia, ESBL organisms, Pseudomonas (imipenem, meropenem) and meningitis (meropenem)
carbapenems.adr: Nausea, diarrhoea, rash, thrombophlebitis, seizures (imipenem at high dose), C. difficile colitis and fungal superinfection; imipenem is given with cilastatin, which stops its breakdown in the kidney
carbapenems.ci: Allergy to β-lactams; epilepsy and CNS disease (imipenem); valproate (carbapenems lower its level and cause seizures); reduce dose in renal failure

aminoglycoside-antibiotics.moa: Bind the 30S ribosomal subunit, causing misreading and blocking protein synthesis (bactericidal, concentration-dependent, with a post-antibiotic effect); they need oxygen to enter bacteria, so they do not work on anaerobes
aminoglycoside-antibiotics.uses: Serious Gram-negative infection and sepsis; endocarditis (with penicillin); tuberculosis (streptomycin, amikacin, kanamycin); plague and tularaemia; neomycin for gut preparation and hepatic coma; topical use in eye and ear; gentamicin is given once daily
aminoglycoside-antibiotics.adr: Nephrotoxicity, ototoxicity (vestibular and cochlear, irreversible), neuromuscular blockade and rash; blood levels (peak and trough) need monitoring
aminoglycoside-antibiotics.ci: Pregnancy (foetal deafness), myasthenia gravis, renal impairment (reduce dose), and with other nephrotoxic or ototoxic drugs (loop diuretics, vancomycin, cisplatin, amphotericin B)

tetracyclines.moa: Bind the 30S ribosomal subunit and block attachment of aminoacyl-tRNA, stopping protein synthesis (bacteriostatic)
tetracyclines.uses: Rickettsial infection (typhus, scrub typhus), chlamydia, cholera, brucellosis, Lyme disease, mycoplasma, acne vulgaris, malaria prophylaxis (doxycycline), leptospirosis, plague, anthrax, H. pylori regimens, periodontitis
tetracyclines.adr: Nausea, vomiting, oesophageal ulceration, discoloured teeth and enamel hypoplasia in children, impaired bone growth, photosensitivity, superinfection, liver injury in pregnancy, vestibular effects (minocycline), benign intracranial hypertension, Fanconi syndrome from outdated tablets
tetracyclines.ci: Pregnancy, breastfeeding, children under 8 years, severe renal failure (except doxycycline) and liver disease; do not take with milk, antacids or iron

chloramphenicol.moa: Binds the 50S ribosomal subunit and blocks peptidyl transferase, stopping protein synthesis (bacteriostatic)
chloramphenicol.uses: Typhoid fever (reserve drug), bacterial meningitis in penicillin-allergic patients, rickettsial infection, brain abscess, eye drops and ear drops
chloramphenicol.adr: Dose-related bone marrow suppression, idiosyncratic aplastic anaemia, grey baby syndrome in neonates (vomiting, cyanosis, collapse), neuritis, nausea, haemolysis in G6PD deficiency and interactions with phenytoin and warfarin
chloramphenicol.ci: Neonates and premature babies, pregnancy near term, bone marrow disease, liver disease and porphyria; reserve for serious infection

macrolide-antibiotics.moa: Bind the 50S ribosomal subunit and block translocation (bacteriostatic); azithromycin and clarithromycin have a wider spectrum; erythromycin also acts as a motilin agonist
macrolide-antibiotics.uses: Respiratory infection and atypical pneumonia (mycoplasma, legionella, chlamydia), diphtheria, pertussis, streptococcal infection in penicillin allergy, H. pylori (clarithromycin), trachoma, genital chlamydia (azithromycin), Mycobacterium avium (clarithromycin, azithromycin), gastroparesis (erythromycin)
macrolide-antibiotics.adr: Nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, cholestatic hepatitis (erythromycin estolate), QT prolongation and arrhythmias, ototoxicity at high dose and thrombophlebitis; erythromycin and clarithromycin inhibit CYP3A4 and raise levels of theophylline, warfarin, carbamazepine and statins
macrolide-antibiotics.ci: Liver disease, prolonged QT, and with terfenadine, cisapride, pimozide, ergot alkaloids and statins; clarithromycin in pregnancy; myasthenia gravis

lincosamide-antibiotics.moa: Clindamycin and lincomycin bind the 50S ribosomal subunit and block protein synthesis (bacteriostatic)
lincosamide-antibiotics.uses: Anaerobic infection (Bacteroides), skin and soft tissue infection, osteomyelitis, MRSA skin infection, pelvic infection, dental prophylaxis in penicillin allergy, toxoplasmosis, bacterial vaginosis and malaria (with quinine)
lincosamide-antibiotics.adr: Diarrhoea and pseudomembranous colitis from C. difficile, rash, nausea, neuromuscular blockade and jaundice
lincosamide-antibiotics.ci: History of colitis, lincosamide allergy and liver disease; not for meningitis because of poor CSF penetration

aminocyclitol-antibiotic.moa: Spectinomycin binds the 30S ribosomal subunit and stops protein synthesis (bacteriostatic, without causing misreading)
aminocyclitol-antibiotic.uses: Gonorrhoea in patients allergic to penicillin or with resistant organisms (single intramuscular dose)
aminocyclitol-antibiotic.adr: Pain at the injection site, nausea, dizziness, fever, rash and reduced urine output; unlike the aminoglycosides it is not nephrotoxic or ototoxic
aminocyclitol-antibiotic.ci: Hypersensitivity; not effective in pharyngeal gonorrhoea or syphilis; use in pregnancy only if essential

glycopeptide-antibiotics.moa: Vancomycin and teicoplanin bind the D-Ala-D-Ala end of cell wall precursors and block transglycosylation and cell wall synthesis (bactericidal, Gram-positive bacteria only)
glycopeptide-antibiotics.uses: MRSA infection, serious infection with penicillin-resistant Gram-positive organisms, endocarditis, C. difficile colitis (oral vancomycin) and surgical prophylaxis in MRSA carriers or in allergy
glycopeptide-antibiotics.adr: Red man syndrome (flushing from histamine release with rapid infusion), nephrotoxicity, ototoxicity, thrombophlebitis and neutropenia
glycopeptide-antibiotics.ci: Hypersensitivity; renal impairment (adjust the dose and monitor levels); with other nephrotoxic or ototoxic drugs; infuse slowly over at least 60 minutes

oxazolidinone.moa: Linezolid binds the 50S ribosomal subunit and blocks formation of the initiation complex for protein synthesis (a different site, so there is little cross-resistance)
oxazolidinone.uses: Vancomycin-resistant enterococci, MRSA pneumonia and skin infection, and drug-resistant tuberculosis
oxazolidinone.adr: Myelosuppression (thrombocytopenia and anaemia) with long use, peripheral and optic neuropathy, lactic acidosis, diarrhoea, nausea, serotonin syndrome (weak MAO inhibition)
oxazolidinone.ci: With SSRIs, MAO inhibitors, pethidine, pseudoephedrine and large amounts of tyramine-rich food; uncontrolled hypertension; monitor blood counts weekly for long courses

polypeptide-antibiotics.moa: Polymyxin B and colistin disrupt the cell membrane of Gram-negative bacteria like detergents; bacitracin blocks recycling of cell wall precursors
polypeptide-antibiotics.uses: Multidrug-resistant Gram-negative infection (colistin as a last resort); topical use on skin, eye and ear (polymyxin B, bacitracin and neomycin combinations); gut decontamination
polypeptide-antibiotics.adr: Nephrotoxicity, neurotoxicity (paraesthesia, dizziness, neuromuscular blockade) and pain on intramuscular injection; bacitracin: nephrotoxicity if absorbed
polypeptide-antibiotics.ci: Renal impairment, myasthenia gravis, with other nephrotoxic or neurotoxic drugs, and systemic use of bacitracin; in pregnancy only if essential

urinary-antiseptics.moa: Nitrofurantoin is activated inside bacteria and damages their DNA and proteins; methenamine releases formaldehyde in acid urine; nalidixic acid inhibits DNA gyrase; all reach a high concentration in urine but not in blood or tissues
urinary-antiseptics.uses: Uncomplicated cystitis and prevention of recurrent urinary infection; not for pyelonephritis, prostatitis or septicaemia
urinary-antiseptics.adr: Nitrofurantoin: nausea, brown urine, peripheral neuropathy, haemolysis in G6PD deficiency, and pulmonary fibrosis and hepatitis with long use; methenamine: bladder irritation and crystals with sulfonamides; nalidixic acid: photosensitivity and raised intracranial pressure in children
urinary-antiseptics.ci: Nitrofurantoin: renal failure, G6PD deficiency, newborns and term pregnancy; methenamine: with sulfonamides and in severe liver or kidney disease; avoid alkalinising the urine

antitubercular-drugs.moa: Rifampicin blocks RNA polymerase; isoniazid inhibits mycolic acid synthesis; pyrazinamide acts in the acid environment inside macrophages (mechanism uncertain); ethambutol blocks arabinosyl transferase; streptomycin blocks protein synthesis; second line drugs include fluoroquinolones, ethionamide, cycloserine, PAS, capreomycin, kanamycin and amikacin
antitubercular-drugs.uses: Tuberculosis: two months of rifampicin, isoniazid, pyrazinamide and ethambutol, then rifampicin and isoniazid for four months; MDR-TB with bedaquiline, linezolid and others; isoniazid prophylaxis in contacts and in HIV
antitubercular-drugs.adr: Isoniazid: hepatitis, peripheral neuropathy (give pyridoxine) and lupus; rifampicin: hepatitis, orange body fluids, flu-like syndrome and enzyme induction; pyrazinamide: hepatotoxicity and hyperuricaemia; ethambutol: optic neuritis (check colour vision); streptomycin: vestibular and renal damage
antitubercular-drugs.ci: Active liver disease; ethambutol in optic neuritis and in young children who cannot report vision changes; pyrazinamide in gout and porphyria; streptomycin in pregnancy and myasthenia; rifampicin lowers the effect of contraceptive pills, warfarin and antiretrovirals

antitubercular-drugs-2.moa: The same drugs grouped by WHO priority for drug-resistant disease: Group A fluoroquinolones, bedaquiline and linezolid; Group B clofazimine and cycloserine; Group C the others
antitubercular-drugs-2.uses: Multidrug-resistant and extensively drug-resistant tuberculosis, with regimens chosen by sensitivity testing
antitubercular-drugs-2.adr: Drug-specific: QT prolongation (bedaquiline, fluoroquinolones, clofazimine), myelosuppression and neuropathy (linezolid), psychosis and depression (cycloserine), hypothyroidism and GI upset (ethionamide, PAS), nephrotoxicity and deafness (injectables) and skin discolouration (clofazimine)
antitubercular-drugs-2.ci: Those of each drug; pregnancy (injectables, ethionamide); uncorrected electrolytes with QT-prolonging drugs; needs specialist supervision and long courses (9 to 20 months)

antileprotic-drugs.moa: Dapsone (a sulfone) blocks folate synthesis; rifampicin blocks RNA polymerase and is rapidly bactericidal; clofazimine binds DNA and is also anti-inflammatory; ofloxacin, minocycline and clarithromycin are other active drugs
antileprotic-drugs.uses: Leprosy: paucibacillary (dapsone and rifampicin, 6 months) and multibacillary (dapsone, rifampicin and clofazimine, 12 months); lepra reactions are treated with steroids, clofazimine or thalidomide
antileprotic-drugs.adr: Dapsone: haemolytic anaemia and methaemoglobinaemia (G6PD), rash, hypersensitivity syndrome and neuropathy; clofazimine: red-brown skin discolouration, ichthyosis and abdominal pain; rifampicin: as in tuberculosis; lepra reactions may worsen early in treatment
antileprotic-drugs.ci: Dapsone: G6PD deficiency and severe anaemia; rifampicin: liver disease; clofazimine: severe abdominal symptoms; thalidomide: pregnancy and women of child-bearing potential

antifungal-drugs.moa: Polyenes (amphotericin B, nystatin) bind ergosterol and form pores in the fungal membrane; azoles (fluconazole, itraconazole, voriconazole, ketoconazole, clotrimazole) block ergosterol synthesis (CYP51); allylamines (terbinafine) block squalene epoxidase; echinocandins (caspofungin) block β-glucan synthesis; flucytosine blocks nucleic acid synthesis; griseofulvin inhibits mitosis
antifungal-drugs.uses: Candidiasis (fluconazole, nystatin, clotrimazole); cryptococcal meningitis (amphotericin B with flucytosine); invasive aspergillosis (voriconazole); mucormycosis (amphotericin B); dermatophyte and nail infection (terbinafine, itraconazole, griseofulvin); systemic mycoses
antifungal-drugs.adr: Amphotericin B: fever, chills, nephrotoxicity, hypokalaemia and anaemia; azoles: nausea, liver injury and many CYP interactions, with ketoconazole: gynaecomastia and adrenal suppression, voriconazole: visual disturbance; terbinafine: taste change and hepatitis; flucytosine: bone marrow suppression; griseofulvin: headache and photosensitivity
antifungal-drugs.ci: Azoles in pregnancy and liver disease, and with terfenadine, cisapride and some statins; ketoconazole in liver disease and long QT; griseofulvin in porphyria and pregnancy; amphotericin B with other nephrotoxic drugs; terbinafine in severe liver disease

non-retroviral-antiviral-drugs.moa: Aciclovir, valaciclovir and famciclovir are phosphorylated by viral thymidine kinase and block viral DNA polymerase; ganciclovir and foscarnet act on CMV polymerase; oseltamivir and zanamivir block neuraminidase; ribavirin, sofosbuvir and others act on RNA polymerase (hepatitis C); tenofovir and entecavir inhibit hepatitis B polymerase; interferons enhance antiviral immunity
non-retroviral-antiviral-drugs.uses: Herpes simplex and zoster, genital herpes, CMV retinitis, influenza, hepatitis B and C, RSV (ribavirin) and COVID-19 (remdesivir, nirmatrelvir)
non-retroviral-antiviral-drugs.adr: Aciclovir: nausea, headache and renal crystals if given rapidly IV; ganciclovir: bone marrow suppression; foscarnet: nephrotoxicity and electrolyte loss; oseltamivir: nausea; ribavirin: haemolytic anaemia and teratogenicity; interferon: flu-like illness, depression and cytopenias
non-retroviral-antiviral-drugs.ci: Ribavirin: pregnancy; ganciclovir: low neutrophil or platelet counts and pregnancy; aciclovir: reduce the dose in renal impairment; interferon: autoimmune disease and severe depression

antiretrovirus-drugs.moa: NRTIs (zidovudine, lamivudine, tenofovir, abacavir) and NNRTIs (efavirenz, nevirapine) block reverse transcriptase; protease inhibitors (lopinavir, atazanavir, darunavir, ritonavir) block viral maturation; integrase inhibitors (dolutegravir, raltegravir) block DNA integration; entry inhibitors (enfuvirtide, maraviroc) block fusion or CCR5
antiretrovirus-drugs.uses: HIV infection (at least three drugs together, ART), prevention of mother-to-child transmission, post-exposure and pre-exposure prophylaxis, and hepatitis B (lamivudine, tenofovir)
antiretrovirus-drugs.adr: Zidovudine: anaemia and myopathy; tenofovir: renal toxicity and bone loss; abacavir: hypersensitivity (HLA-B*5701); efavirenz: vivid dreams and psychiatric effects; nevirapine: rash and hepatitis; protease inhibitors: lipodystrophy, diabetes, GI upset and many CYP interactions; dolutegravir: weight gain and insomnia; immune reconstitution syndrome
antiretrovirus-drugs.ci: Abacavir in HLA-B*5701 positive patients; nevirapine in women with a high CD4 count; efavirenz in psychiatric illness; ritonavir-boosted drugs with CYP3A4 substrates; tenofovir in renal impairment; screen for TB before starting; adherence is essential

antimalarial-drugs.moa: Chloroquine and quinine accumulate in the parasite's food vacuole and block haem detoxification; artemisinins generate free radicals; primaquine acts on liver hypnozoites and gametocytes; atovaquone-proguanil and pyrimethamine-sulfadoxine block folate synthesis; mefloquine acts on blood schizonts
antimalarial-drugs.uses: Treatment of malaria (artemisinin combination therapy for falciparum, chloroquine for vivax, artesunate or quinine for severe malaria); radical cure of vivax and ovale (primaquine); chemoprophylaxis (mefloquine, doxycycline, atovaquone-proguanil, chloroquine)
antimalarial-drugs.adr: Chloroquine: nausea, itching and retinopathy on long use; quinine: cinchonism (tinnitus, deafness, headache), hypoglycaemia and hypotension; primaquine: haemolysis in G6PD deficiency; mefloquine: neuropsychiatric effects; artemisinins: usually well tolerated, delayed haemolysis; sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine: rash and Stevens-Johnson syndrome
antimalarial-drugs.ci: Primaquine: G6PD deficiency and pregnancy; mefloquine: psychiatric illness and epilepsy; quinine: optic neuritis and tinnitus; chloroquine: caution in retinal disease and psoriasis; doxycycline in pregnancy and children; sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine: sulfa allergy

antiamoebic-drugs.moa: Metronidazole, tinidazole, secnidazole and ornidazole are reduced inside anaerobes and damage their DNA (tissue amoebicides); diloxanide furoate acts in the gut lumen; emetine and chloroquine act on tissue forms
antiamoebic-drugs.uses: Amoebic dysentery and amoebic liver abscess (metronidazole followed by diloxanide to clear cysts), giardiasis, trichomoniasis and anaerobic infection
antiamoebic-drugs.adr: Metronidazole: metallic taste, nausea, headache, disulfiram-like reaction with alcohol, peripheral neuropathy and dark urine; diloxanide: flatulence; emetine: cardiotoxicity and myositis
antiamoebic-drugs.ci: Metronidazole: first trimester of pregnancy (avoid if possible), alcohol use and CNS disease; emetine: heart disease, pregnancy and children; avoid alcohol for 48 hours after a dose

drugs-for-giardiasis.moa: Metronidazole, tinidazole and secnidazole are activated by the parasite and damage its DNA; nitazoxanide and albendazole are alternatives
drugs-for-giardiasis.uses: Giardiasis (a single dose of tinidazole or secnidazole is convenient)
drugs-for-giardiasis.adr: Metallic taste, nausea, headache, dizziness and a disulfiram-like reaction
drugs-for-giardiasis.ci: First trimester of pregnancy, alcohol, blood dyscrasias and neurological disease

drugs-for-trichomoniasis.moa: Nitroimidazoles (metronidazole, tinidazole, secnidazole) damage the DNA of Trichomonas vaginalis; clotrimazole and others help local symptoms
drugs-for-trichomoniasis.uses: Trichomonas vaginitis and urethritis (treat the partner too) and bacterial vaginosis
drugs-for-trichomoniasis.adr: Nausea, metallic taste, headache, vaginal irritation and a disulfiram-like reaction
drugs-for-trichomoniasis.ci: First trimester of pregnancy, alcohol and neurological disease; partners must be treated to prevent reinfection

drugs-for-leishmaniasis.moa: Sodium stibogluconate (antimonials) interfere with the parasite's energy metabolism; liposomal amphotericin B binds ergosterol; miltefosine disrupts membrane signalling; paromomycin blocks protein synthesis; pentamidine acts on DNA
drugs-for-leishmaniasis.uses: Visceral leishmaniasis (kala-azar), post kala-azar dermal leishmaniasis, cutaneous and mucocutaneous leishmaniasis; single-dose liposomal amphotericin B is now preferred in India
drugs-for-leishmaniasis.adr: Antimonials: cardiotoxicity (QT), pancreatitis, nephrotoxicity and myalgia; amphotericin B: infusion reactions and kidney injury; miltefosine: nausea, vomiting and teratogenicity; paromomycin: nephrotoxicity and ototoxicity; pentamidine: hypoglycaemia, diabetes and hypotension
drugs-for-leishmaniasis.ci: Miltefosine: pregnancy and breastfeeding (needs contraception); antimonials: heart, kidney and liver disease and pregnancy; paromomycin: renal impairment

anthelmintic-drugs.moa: Albendazole and mebendazole block tubulin polymerisation and glucose uptake; pyrantel causes spastic paralysis by depolarising the muscle; piperazine causes flaccid paralysis; praziquantel increases calcium entry and paralyses the worm; ivermectin opens glutamate-gated chloride channels; DEC (diethylcarbamazine) acts on microfilariae; niclosamide uncouples oxidative phosphorylation
anthelmintic-drugs.uses: Roundworm, hookworm, whipworm and pinworm (albendazole, mebendazole, pyrantel); tapeworm and neurocysticercosis (praziquantel, albendazole); hydatid disease (albendazole); strongyloides and scabies (ivermectin); filariasis (DEC, ivermectin, albendazole); schistosomiasis (praziquantel)
anthelmintic-drugs.adr: Usually mild: nausea, abdominal pain, headache and dizziness; albendazole: raised liver enzymes and marrow suppression with long courses; ivermectin and DEC: Mazzotti reaction (fever, itch, hypotension) from dying microfilariae; praziquantel: drowsiness; neurocysticercosis is treated with steroids to blunt inflammation
anthelmintic-drugs.ci: Albendazole and mebendazole in pregnancy and children under 2 years; DEC and ivermectin in loiasis (encephalopathy risk); piperazine in epilepsy and kidney disease; steroid cover in neurocysticercosis

anticancer-drugs.moa: Alkylating agents (cyclophosphamide, ifosfamide, melphalan, chlorambucil, busulfan, dacarbazine, temozolomide) add alkyl groups to DNA and cause cross-links; platinum drugs (cisplatin, carboplatin, oxaliplatin) form DNA adducts; antimetabolites copy normal building blocks: methotrexate (DHFR), 5-fluorouracil and capecitabine (thymidylate synthase), 6-mercaptopurine and thioguanine (purine synthesis), cytarabine and gemcitabine (DNA polymerase), hydroxyurea (ribonucleotide reductase)
anticancer-drugs.uses: Leukaemias, lymphomas, breast, ovarian, lung, testicular, colorectal and bladder cancer; methotrexate also in choriocarcinoma, psoriasis and rheumatoid arthritis; cyclophosphamide in autoimmune disease; temozolomide in glioma; hydroxyurea in sickle cell disease and CML
anticancer-drugs.adr: Common to cytotoxics: bone marrow suppression, nausea and vomiting, mucositis, alopecia, infertility, teratogenicity and second cancers; cyclophosphamide: haemorrhagic cystitis (mesna protects); cisplatin: nephrotoxicity, ototoxicity, neuropathy and severe vomiting; carboplatin: marrow suppression; busulfan: pulmonary fibrosis; methotrexate: mucositis, liver and lung toxicity (folinic acid rescue); 5-FU: diarrhoea and hand-foot syndrome; cytarabine: cerebellar toxicity
anticancer-drugs.ci: Pregnancy, active serious infection and severe bone marrow depression; cisplatin in renal impairment and hearing loss; methotrexate with NSAIDs and trimethoprim and in renal failure; allopurinol with 6-MP (reduce the dose); live vaccines; check blood counts before each cycle

anticancer-drugs-2.moa: Vinca alkaloids (vincristine, vinblastine, vinorelbine) stop microtubule assembly; taxanes (paclitaxel, docetaxel) stabilise microtubules; etoposide blocks topoisomerase II; irinotecan and topotecan block topoisomerase I; antibiotics: doxorubicin and daunorubicin (intercalate DNA, topoisomerase II, free radicals), bleomycin (DNA strand breaks), dactinomycin and mitomycin C; miscellaneous: L-asparaginase and hydroxyurea
anticancer-drugs-2.uses: Lymphomas and leukaemias (vincristine, anthracyclines); breast, ovarian and lung cancer (taxanes); testicular and small cell lung cancer (etoposide, bleomycin); colorectal cancer (irinotecan); sarcomas, Wilms' tumour, Kaposi sarcoma and Hodgkin lymphoma (ABVD)
anticancer-drugs-2.adr: Vincristine: peripheral neuropathy, constipation and SIADH; vinblastine: marrow suppression; paclitaxel: hypersensitivity, neuropathy, neutropenia and alopecia; doxorubicin: cardiomyopathy (dose related), red urine, extravasation necrosis and alopecia; bleomycin: pulmonary fibrosis and skin pigmentation; irinotecan: severe diarrhoea; etoposide: marrow suppression; asparaginase: allergy, pancreatitis and clotting problems
anticancer-drugs-2.ci: Doxorubicin: heart disease and cumulative dose above about 450 to 550 mg/m2; bleomycin: lung disease and high oxygen exposure; vincristine: never intrathecal (fatal); paclitaxel: pre-medicate with steroids and antihistamines; all: pregnancy, severe marrow depression and active infection

anticancer-drugs-3.moa: Tyrosine kinase inhibitors (imatinib, dasatinib, sunitinib, sorafenib) block BCR-ABL, KIT and other kinases; EGFR inhibitors (erlotinib, gefitinib); angiogenesis inhibitors (bevacizumab, thalidomide); proteasome inhibitor (bortezomib); monoclonal antibodies (rituximab to CD20, trastuzumab to HER2, cetuximab to EGFR); hormonal drugs deprive hormone-dependent tumours: tamoxifen and other SERMs, fulvestrant, aromatase inhibitors, antiandrogens, GnRH analogues, progestins and glucocorticoids
anticancer-drugs-3.uses: Chronic myeloid leukaemia and GIST (imatinib); HER2-positive breast cancer (trastuzumab); non-Hodgkin lymphoma (rituximab); EGFR-mutant lung cancer (erlotinib, gefitinib); renal and liver cancer (sunitinib, sorafenib); multiple myeloma (bortezomib); colorectal cancer (bevacizumab); hormone-positive breast cancer (tamoxifen, letrozole); prostate cancer (bicalutamide, GnRH analogues); lymphoid cancers (prednisolone)
anticancer-drugs-3.adr: Imatinib: fluid retention, nausea and cytopenias; EGFR inhibitors: acneiform rash and diarrhoea; bevacizumab: bleeding, hypertension, poor wound healing and perforation; trastuzumab: cardiotoxicity; rituximab: infusion reactions and hepatitis B reactivation; bortezomib: neuropathy; sunitinib: hand-foot syndrome and hypertension; tamoxifen: hot flushes, thrombosis and endometrial cancer; aromatase inhibitors: bone loss; GnRH analogues: hot flushes and flare
anticancer-drugs-3.ci: Trastuzumab: reduced cardiac function (check the ejection fraction); rituximab: active hepatitis B; bevacizumab: recent surgery or bleeding; tamoxifen: thromboembolism and pregnancy; imatinib: pregnancy; check the target (receptor or mutation) before use

immunosuppressant-drugs.moa: Calcineurin inhibitors (cyclosporine, tacrolimus) block IL-2 production in T cells; mTOR inhibitors (sirolimus, everolimus) block T-cell proliferation; antiproliferatives (azathioprine, mycophenolate, methotrexate, cyclophosphamide, leflunomide) stop lymphocyte DNA synthesis; glucocorticoids suppress cytokines; biologics (basiliximab, antithymocyte globulin, rituximab, anti-TNF drugs) target specific immune cells or cytokines
immunosuppressant-drugs.uses: Prevention of organ transplant rejection and graft versus host disease; autoimmune diseases (lupus, rheumatoid arthritis, nephritis, inflammatory bowel disease); psoriasis
immunosuppressant-drugs.adr: Infection (including opportunistic infection and reactivated TB), lymphomas and skin cancers; cyclosporine: nephrotoxicity, hypertension, gum hyperplasia, hirsutism and tremor; tacrolimus: nephrotoxicity, diabetes and neurotoxicity; azathioprine: bone marrow suppression and hepatitis; mycophenolate: diarrhoea and leukopenia; sirolimus: hyperlipidaemia, poor wound healing and mouth ulcers
immunosuppressant-drugs.ci: Active serious infection; live vaccines; pregnancy (mycophenolate, methotrexate, cyclophosphamide); azathioprine with allopurinol (reduce the dose by about 75 percent); cyclosporine and tacrolimus with nephrotoxic drugs and CYP3A4 inhibitors or inducers; monitor blood levels

chelating-agents.moa: Form stable, soluble complexes with metals which are then excreted in urine or bile: dimercaprol (BAL), succimer (DMSA) and DMPS bind arsenic, mercury, lead and gold; calcium disodium EDTA binds lead; desferrioxamine and deferasirox bind iron; penicillamine and trientine bind copper; deferiprone binds iron
chelating-agents.uses: Lead, arsenic and mercury poisoning; iron overdose and transfusion iron overload; Wilson's disease (penicillamine, trientine, zinc); thalassaemia
chelating-agents.adr: Dimercaprol: hypertension, tachycardia, sweating, painful injection and haemolysis in G6PD deficiency; EDTA: nephrotoxicity, hypocalcaemia (use the calcium salt) and zinc loss; desferrioxamine: hearing and eye toxicity, infusion hypotension and Yersinia infection; penicillamine: rash, nephrotic syndrome, bone marrow suppression and lupus; deferiprone: agranulocytosis
chelating-agents.ci: Dimercaprol: iron, cadmium and selenium poisoning (toxic complexes), liver damage and peanut-oil allergy; EDTA: renal failure and cerebral oedema with rapid infusion; penicillamine: penicillin allergy, pregnancy and lupus; deferiprone: neutropenia

locally-acting-drugs-on-skin-and-mucous-.moa: Demulcents soothe; emollients hydrate the skin; adsorbents and protectives (zinc oxide, talc, calamine) cover and dry; astringents precipitate proteins to dry and tighten tissue; counterirritants (methyl salicylate, menthol, camphor) cause redness and relieve deeper pain; keratolytics (salicylic acid, urea, benzoyl peroxide) soften and shed keratin; caustics (silver nitrate, podophyllin, trichloroacetic acid) destroy tissue; retinoids, tar, anthralin and vitamin D analogues treat psoriasis and acne
locally-acting-drugs-on-skin-and-mucous-.uses: Dry skin and eczema (emollients), itching and weeping dermatoses (calamine, astringents), muscle and joint pain (counterirritants), warts and corns (keratolytics, caustics), psoriasis, acne, scabies and fungal skin infection
locally-acting-drugs-on-skin-and-mucous-.adr: Contact dermatitis, irritation, burning, dryness, photosensitivity (tar, retinoids, psoralens), systemic absorption of salicylic acid (salicylism) and tar, and skin discolouration; oral retinoids: teratogenic
locally-acting-drugs-on-skin-and-mucous-.ci: Open wounds, broken or inflamed skin, mucous membranes and eyes (counterirritants, keratolytics, caustics); large body areas in children; podophyllin and retinoids in pregnancy; avoid heat over counterirritants

drugs-for-acne-vulgaris.moa: Benzoyl peroxide kills C. acnes and is keratolytic; topical retinoids (tretinoin, adapalene) normalise follicle keratinisation; topical antibiotics (clindamycin, erythromycin), azelaic acid and salicylic acid reduce bacteria and comedones; oral antibiotics (doxycycline, minocycline, azithromycin), isotretinoin (shrinks sebaceous glands), antiandrogens (cyproterone, spironolactone) and combined pills treat severe or hormonal acne
drugs-for-acne-vulgaris.uses: Mild acne (benzoyl peroxide, retinoid), moderate acne (add an antibiotic), severe nodulocystic or scarring acne (isotretinoin) and hormonal acne in women
drugs-for-acne-vulgaris.adr: Topical: dryness, redness, peeling, bleaching of fabric (benzoyl peroxide) and photosensitivity; isotretinoin: severe teratogenicity, dry lips and skin, raised triglycerides and liver enzymes, headache, muscle pain and mood concerns; tetracyclines: photosensitivity and GI upset
drugs-for-acne-vulgaris.ci: Isotretinoin: pregnancy (absolute, needs contraception), liver disease, hyperlipidaemia and with tetracyclines (intracranial hypertension); tetracyclines in pregnancy and children under 8 years; topical retinoids in pregnancy

antiseptics-and-disinfectants.moa: Denature proteins, disrupt membranes or oxidise cell components: phenols (chloroxylenol, cresol, hexachlorophene), oxidising agents (hydrogen peroxide, potassium permanganate), halogens (iodine, povidone-iodine, chlorine compounds), chlorhexidine, quaternary ammonium compounds (cetrimide, benzalkonium), alcohols (ethanol, isopropanol), aldehydes (formaldehyde, glutaraldehyde), heavy metals (silver nitrate) and acids
antiseptics-and-disinfectants.uses: Antiseptics for skin, wounds, mouth and hand hygiene; disinfectants for instruments, surfaces, excreta and water (chlorine); sterilisation of heat-sensitive equipment (glutaraldehyde); pre-operative skin preparation
antiseptics-and-disinfectants.adr: Skin irritation and sensitisation, burns, iodine sensitivity, thyroid effects with repeated use, chlorhexidine anaphylaxis, absorption and neurotoxicity of hexachlorophene in infants, tissue damage if used in deep wounds, and corrosive injury from concentrated solutions
antiseptics-and-disinfectants.ci: Povidone-iodine in iodine allergy, thyroid disease, newborns and pregnancy; alcohol on open wounds and mucous membranes and near diathermy; hexachlorophene in infants and burns; chlorhexidine in the eye, ear and meninges; disinfectants are not for use on living tissue

ectoparasiticides.moa: Permethrin acts on parasite sodium channels and causes paralysis; benzyl benzoate is toxic to mites and lice; gamma benzene hexachloride (lindane) and malathion cause neurotoxicity in the parasite; crotamiton and sulphur kill mites; ivermectin acts on glutamate-gated chloride channels; dimeticone coats and suffocates lice
ectoparasiticides.uses: Scabies (permethrin 5 percent cream, benzyl benzoate, ivermectin), head lice (permethrin, dimeticone, malathion), pediculosis pubis (crab lice) and demodex
ectoparasiticides.adr: Skin irritation, burning, itching and dermatitis; lindane: neurotoxicity and seizures if swallowed or absorbed; benzyl benzoate: stinging, especially in children; itching after scabies persists for weeks
ectoparasiticides.ci: Lindane in infants, pregnancy, seizure disorders and on broken skin; undiluted benzyl benzoate in children; malathion on open skin; avoid the eyes; treat the whole household together

vaccines.moa: Stimulate active immunity and memory cells without causing the disease: killed (inactivated) vaccines, live attenuated vaccines (stronger and longer-lasting immunity), toxoids (inactivated toxins such as tetanus and diphtheria), subunit, conjugate and recombinant vaccines, and combined vaccines
vaccines.uses: Prevention of infectious diseases following the national immunisation schedule: BCG, OPV and IPV, hepatitis B, DPT, pentavalent, rotavirus, pneumococcal, measles, MR, MMR, Japanese encephalitis, typhoid, rabies, HPV, influenza and COVID-19; booster doses
vaccines.adr: Mild local pain, redness, swelling, fever and irritability; rarely anaphylaxis; BCG: local ulcer and lymphadenitis; OPV: vaccine-associated paralytic polio (rare); MMR: rash, febrile seizure and rare thrombocytopenia; rotavirus: intussusception (rare)
vaccines.ci: Live vaccines in pregnancy, severe immunodeficiency, high-dose steroids and cancer therapy; a severe allergic reaction to a previous dose or a component; acute severe febrile illness (postpone); encephalopathy after a previous pertussis dose; keep the cold chain

antisera-and-immune-globulins.moa: Provide ready-made antibodies for immediate passive immunity or to neutralise toxins and venoms; antisera from horses are heterologous; human immune globulins are homologous and safer
antisera-and-immune-globulins.uses: Snake bite (polyvalent antivenom), scorpion sting, tetanus (human tetanus immune globulin), diphtheria antitoxin, rabies immune globulin with vaccine, hepatitis B immune globulin (newborns of HBsAg-positive mothers), anti-D (Rh-negative mothers), botulism, and post-exposure prophylaxis of measles and varicella
antisera-and-immune-globulins.adr: Horse serum: anaphylaxis, serum sickness (1 to 2 weeks later), fever and rash; human immune globulin: local pain, fever and rare allergy; IV immune globulin: headache, renal injury and thrombosis
antisera-and-immune-globulins.ci: Test dose for horse serum and keep adrenaline ready; IgA deficiency (for some products); a previous severe reaction to horse serum; give live vaccines at least three months after an immune globulin
